_doc: Routing, cost and quota constants for the orchestrator loop (docs/rearchitecture/DESIGN-orchestrator-loop.md sections 8 and 9). Read by budget.py and plan_wave.py. A constant changes only by an explicit edit that restates its date and source.

calibration.source: waves 1011-1015: weekly-meter movement against the subagent tokens the Workflow tool reported per wave (orchestrator session, 2026-10-04). The Workflow's token count and the telemetry sum below may not be the same measure: refit from units.jsonl and usage_report.py (kb/Work PB1981 item 9; design open decision D6).
calibration.tokens_per_point_frontier_source: fable and mythos: 2.5x the Opus rate, the published price ratio ($10/$50 against $4/$20 per MTok; kb/Work R69, 2026-10-06), until a meter reading refits it
calibration.session_pct_per_weekly_pct_source: a guess (design open decision D7) until two readings inside one session window measure it

quota.weekly_cap_source: owner 2026-10-07: run ALL work with the appropriate models up to 85 % of the weekly quota, then PAUSE (kb/Work R69 section 6); it replaced the 98 % ceiling of 2026-10-02 and the 44 % cap on other work of 2026-10-05

routing._owner_approval_why: A note whose body says its work needs a frontier model (Fable, Mythos) under the owner's approval is never planned: that approval is per dispatch (MANDATORY-PRACTICES P1), which an unattended wave cannot obtain, so the planner lists the note as waiting and the attended session asks. First case: PB2118, R1's authorship (kb/Work R69 section 4, PB2120, 2026-10-07).
routing._why: Opus where the work is design-heavy (OO, grammar), where a note says a design question is open, or where a note has already failed twice (a note that fails twice is a task-spec problem, kb/Work PB1981). Opus also for the legacy-retirement cuts (CI and gate wiring carry the CI invariant) and the architecture review's R0/R1 items (kb/Work R69). Fable and Mythos are never values here: each needs explicit owner approval per dispatch (owner 2026-10-02; R69 2026-10-06).

cost.source: seeded 2026-10-04 so that a five-note group costs about 0.4 weekly points on either model, a lander about 0.3, and a six-group wave of five-note groups about 3 points with its landers, matching waves 1011-1015 (kb/Work PB1981: a six-group wave already costs about 3 weekly points); refit from units.jsonl

campaign._why: plan_wave.py --cluster (kb/Work PB2120): a campaign note's code sites are whatever it names, so its notes are clustered over the whole tree, not .agent-fleet.json's src/Cobol.Net.* (which the fix lane keeps). Project files (.csproj, .props, .targets) are not sites: their dotted names (Cobol.Net.Cli.csproj) make fix_clusters read every `Cobol.Net` in a note as a Type.Member reference to the first one indexed (measured on PB2108, 2026-10-07). exclude_dir names directories that hold corpora or generated output, never a fix site: the GnuCOBOL corpus (tests/external), the conformance programs and goldens, gate run output, and the frozen evidence records under docs/.

wave.max_groups_source: waves 1011-1015 ran 5 to 7 groups; the budget is the governor, this bounds the train count
